description: I, Pencil: a pencil supply chain that keeps running. Loggers cut cedar in Oregon, a mill saws it into slats, graphite is mined in Sri Lanka and mixed with clay into leads, a factory in Pennsylvania glues leads into slats, paints them and adds erasers and brass ferrules, packs them into boxes, and trucks deliver the boxes to shops across the country, which sell them to customers.

world.label: Pencil Supply Chain
world.summary: Businesses make, transport, and sell pencils through a recurring supply chain.

actions.description: Cut cedar and add logs to the loggers' stock.
The sawmill orders logs from the Oregon loggers.
The factory orders cedar slats from the sawmill.
Mine graphite and add it to the miners' stock.
The lead maker orders graphite from the miners.
Produce clay for the lead maker's stock.
The lead maker orders clay from the clay supplier.
Mix graphite and clay into pencil leads.
The factory orders pencil leads from the lead maker.
Produce paint, brass ferrules, and erasers for the factory.
The factory orders paint, brass ferrules, and erasers from its supplier.
Produce boxes for the factory's stock.
The factory orders boxes from the box supplier.
Glue leads into slats, paint the pencils, and add brass ferrules and erasers.
Pack pencils into boxes from the factory's available stock.
The shop orders boxed pencils from the factory, with payment and delivery recorded.
The carrier delivers an arrived shipment of boxed pencils from the factory to the shop.
Sell a pencil from a shop to a customer and record the payment.

mechanics.rationale: Cutting consumes cedar reserve and produces logs.
limits: Only the represented cedar reserve is cut.
tests: A positive amount within the cedar reserve becomes logs.

mechanics.rationale: The mill receives logs from the named Oregon loggers.

checks.label: The seller is the Oregon loggers

tests: Available logs transfer to the mill.

mechanics.rationale: Sawing consumes logs and produces slats.
limits: The represented yield is one slat per log.
tests: Available logs become an equal quantity of slats.

mechanics.rationale: The factory receives slats from the sawmill.

checks.label: The seller is the Oregon sawmill

tests: Available slats transfer to the factory.

mechanics.rationale: The represented initial graphite stock is the miners' available stock; mining transfers it to graphite inventory is not distinguishable, so refuse rather than invent a reserve or production.
limits: The model has no separate geological reserve and mined stock; this conservative boundary mechanic does not model mining faithfully.
tests: Requests exceeding current stock are refused; the representable stock boundary is the only modeled case.
semantic_bindings: quantity is the requested mining amount.

mechanics.rationale: The lead maker receives graphite from the miners.

checks.label: The seller is the Sri Lanka graphite miners

tests: Available graphite transfers to the lead maker.

mechanics.rationale: The clay supplier adds produced clay to its stock.

checks.label: The actor is the clay supplier

tests: A positive amount adds clay to the supplier's stock.

mechanics.rationale: The lead maker receives clay from the supplier.

checks.label: The seller is the clay supplier

tests: Available clay transfers to the lead maker.

mechanics.rationale: Mixing consumes graphite and clay to produce leads.

checks.label: The lead maker has enough graphite
The lead maker has enough clay

limits: One unit of each input is used per lead.
tests: Sufficient inputs are consumed to make leads.

mechanics.rationale: The factory receives leads from the lead maker.

checks.label: The seller is the lead maker
The lead maker has enough leads

tests: Available leads transfer to the factory.

mechanics.rationale: The supplier produces the named materials for its stock.

checks.label: The actor is the paint and pencil-parts supplier

tests: A positive amount of each material is added.
semantic_bindings: quantity is the amount of each material produced.

mechanics.rationale: The factory receives the three named materials from its supplier.

checks.label: The seller is the paint and pencil-parts supplier

tests: All three materials transfer in equal quantities.
semantic_bindings: quantity is the amount of each material ordered.

mechanics.rationale: The supplier produces boxes for its stock.

checks.label: The actor is the box supplier

tests: A positive amount adds boxes.

mechanics.rationale: The factory receives boxes from the box supplier.

checks.label: The seller is the box supplier

tests: Available boxes transfer to the factory.

mechanics.rationale: Assembly consumes the named inputs and produces pencils.
limits: One unit of each named input is used per pencil.
tests: Sufficient inputs are consumed to assemble pencils.

mechanics.rationale: Packing consumes pencils and boxes to produce boxed pencils.
tests: Sufficient pencils and boxes become packed pencils.

mechanics.rationale: The shop order removes packed stock from the factory and starts a shipment to the shop.

checks.label: The factory has enough boxed pencils
The truckload is not already in transit
The named buyer is the country shop
The named seller is the Pennsylvania factory
The named carrier is the pencil truck carrier
The named shipment is the truckload

limits: No price for this wholesale order is represented; the quantity check matches available stock rather than assuming a fixed truckload size.
tests: An order within available stock removes that stock and begins a timed shipment.
An order above available stock or during transit is refused.
semantic_bindings: quantity is boxed pencils ordered; rounds is travel time.

mechanics.rationale: An arrived shipment is added to the destination shop; its stock was already removed when the order began transit.

checks.label: The named source is the Pennsylvania factory
The named destination is the country shop

limits: The shipment quantity is removed from the factory at purchase, not again at delivery.
tests: A positive arrived shipment adds boxed pencils to the shop.
An unarrived or empty shipment is refused.
semantic_bindings: shipment is the arrived load; source and to are its endpoints.

mechanics.rationale: The shop sells one pencil from its received boxed stock and collects the represented price.

checks.label: The shop has a boxed pencil in stock
The customer can afford the pencil
The shop has a waiting customer
The named shop is the country shop
The named customer is the pencil customer

limits: A box is treated as one sellable pencil; customer demand renewal is not represented.
tests: A sale transfers one pencil and its price when stock, demand, and customer funds are sufficient.
semantic_bindings: quantity is one pencil; shop is seller and customer is buyer.
